confirmed.title: The announcement's bubble and command window name the stop chord even when another app holds it, while the spoken line drops it
confirmed.scenario: Another app has already registered Ember's stop chord: Ctrl+Alt+X on Linux, Win+Alt+X on Windows, or Control+Shift+Command+X on macOS. Ember's registration fails, so shortcutsTaken holds the accelerator (main.ts:1486-1488). The user then types "delete build/" and the flow announces `rm -r build` (D4.4). The bubble says "On this computer. It starts in 4 seconds. Ctrl+Alt+X stops everything at once." The command window says "Or press Ctrl+Alt+X to stop everything." Only the spoken line knows the chord isn't Ember's: it says "Press Stop to cancel." A keyboard or screen-reader user who presses the advertised chord during the countdown reaches the other app, not Ember's kill switch, and the dangerous command runs. The Stop buttons still work, so the wrong advice only affects people who use the chord.
confirmed.evidence: Code read: the presenter builds the announcement with a fixed label. presenter.ts:529 sets `this.stopKey = (opts.shortcuts ?? SHORTCUTS.linux).stop.label`, and presenter.ts:848 passes it to `announcement(text, this.where, seconds, this.stopKey)` (target-copy.ts:143-147). The command window does the same: window.ts:360 adds `announceKeys: announceKeyText(o.os)`, and copy.ts:199-201 returns `Or press ${SHORTCUTS[os].stop.label} to stop everything.`. Neither one asks whether Ember holds the key. The spoken path does: main.ts:1799 passes `cancelWords({ killPhrase: voice?.rejectsSpeakers ?? false, stopKey: hasKey(sc.stop.accel) ? sc.stop.say : null })`, where hasKey (main.ts:541) checks shortcutsTaken. Ember already handles a taken key for the settings route (keyboardRoute(key: string | null) in target-copy.ts) and for the card's key hint (deps.keyHint holds only the keys main holds). Ran: I bundled the integration branch's copy functions into /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/xreview/cmdsafety/bundles/copy.cjs and printed each OS with the chord taken. linux: bubble 'On this computer. It starts in 4 seconds. Ctrl+Alt+X stops everything at once.', window 'Or press Ctrl+Alt+X to stop everything.', spoken 'Press Stop to cancel.' win32 and darwin give the same mismatch with Win+Alt+X and Control+Shift+Command+X.
confirmed.cause: fix/cmdwin (#46, #269) added the stop chord to the bubble's announcement and the window's countdown from the static SHORTCUTS table. fix/bubble (#22, #24) moved the bubble text into target-copy's announcement() with cmdwin's chord (merge 1d44566). fix/voice (#251) is the only one that checks whether Ember holds the chord (cancelWords with hasKey), and only for the spoken line. The three wordings of the same announcement disagree.
confirmed.fix: Give the announcement the chord only while Ember holds it, the way cancelWords gets it. Add an option such as `stopKey?: () => string | null` (main: `() => hasKey(sc.stop.accel) ? sc.stop.label : null`), passed through AgentHost to the task presenters, and a matching `stopKey()` hook in CommandWindowOptions next to keyHint. When it is null, announcement() and announceKeyText() leave out the chord sentence and the Stop button is the only route named, as the spoken "Press Stop to cancel." already does. Pin the taken-chord case in ui-copy.test.ts and command-window.test.ts.

verdict.reason:

- **Bubble:** app/main/agent/presenter.ts:529 fixes `stopKey` from the static table (`(opts.shortcuts ?? SHORTCUTS.linux).stop.label`). Every AgentHost presenter is built with `shortcuts: this.sys.shortcuts` (host.ts:621, 622, 703, 1126, 1415). announce() at presenter.ts:848 passes it to announcement() (target-copy.ts:143-147), which always writes "<chord> stops everything at once."
- **Command window:** app/main/commands/window.ts:360 always adds `announceKeys: announceKeyText(o.os)` while an announcement counts down. copy.ts:200-201 returns `Or press ${SHORTCUTS[os].stop.label} to stop everything.` with no taken-key input.

- **No fallback:** nothing elsewhere rewrites the bubble or window text, and no local handler (before-input-event or renderer keydown) catches the stop chord. When another app holds the chord globally, pressing it never reaches Ember.

Ran: I bundled the integration branch's announcement, announceKeyText, cancelWords and SHORTCUTS into /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/xreview/skeptic-stopkey/out.cjs and ran it with the stop accelerator marked taken.

Not already scheduled:

- The merge note "announcement wording ... + stop chord: check what the merge chose" is about the bubble #22 vs cmdwin #46 wording. It does not cover the taken-key case.

confirmed.title: "More time to read and answer" is applied twice to any bubble that waited or was covered, so it stays 100 times its usual time instead of 10
confirmed.scenario: More time is on (readTime 10). Case 1: a task finishes while the user is reading the conversation's answer. Its result (claim "reply") waits, then shows when the answer goes, and stays 885 s instead of 88.5 s. For that time it holds the bubble, so other tasks' progress can't show, and overlay.ts keeps Ember parked (a finished done/idle/error message counts as waiting), so Ember stops following the pointer for about 15 minutes. Case 2: an unasked ssh or WSL offer (OFFER_MS 25 s) that waited behind an answer stays 2500 s, not 250 s, with Ember held still beside its buttons. Case 3: "Hey Ember" that was another word gives an answer back (claimBubble, then releaseBubble), and the answer stays 688 s, not 68 s. Every further cover multiplies by 10 again. Any answer that finished behind a question is affected too.
confirmed.evidence: hideLater() scales the time and stores the scaled value: presenter.ts:666-668 (ms = base*scale), then pendingHide = ms at :670 or hideMs = ms at :671. letGo() copies the scaled hideMs into pendingHide (:615-618). reshow() calls hideLater(this.pendingHide) at :635, which multiplies by the scale again. I ran a scratch vitest file on an export of HEAD (scratchpad/xreview/bubble/tree/test/unit/xreview-readtime.test.ts) with a real BubbleOwner and Presenters, readTime = readTimeOf(true). Results: "offer stayed 2500.01 s on screen (expected 250 s)", "answer stayed 688.01 s after it was given back (expected at most 68 s)", "task result stayed 885 s (expected 88.5 s)". All three fail. The package's own #51 tests only cover bubbles that are on screen at once (presenter.test.ts:902-936).
confirmed.cause: fix/bubble #51 (50ebd22, 8d95111): readTime scaling added inside hideLater, which reshow() and letGo() reuse with already-scaled times. It surfaces in every interaction that makes a bubble wait: the Confirmer's questions, main's claimBubble for Listening… and the kill switch, and the runtime's unasked offers (#14).
confirmed.fix: Scale only once. Split hideLater(base) into hideLater(base) { this.armHide(base * scale) } and armHide(ms), which sets pendingHide or hideTimer/hideMs with no further scaling. reshow() calls this.armHide(this.pendingHide). Add the three cases above to presenter.test.ts.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed the finding on HEAD 4e47b13. The scratch tree's app/main/agent/presenter.ts is identical to the worktree's.

How it happens:
- hideLater(base) multiplies by readTime, which is clamped to 1..10 and is 10 when More time is on (presenter.ts:666-668). It then stores the scaled value, either as pendingHide when the bubble is unseen (:670) or as hideMs (:671).
- letGo() copies the scaled hideMs or pendingHide back into pendingHide (:615-618).
- reshow() calls hideLater(this.pendingHide) (:635), which multiplies by 10 a second time.

Real paths that reach it:
- A bubble that waited behind another: post() at :744, outcome/idle at :880 and :1017, then reshow when the bubble frees up.
- An answer covered by main's claimBubble: host.ts:721-722 runs owner.claim (which calls covered.letGo(), presenter.ts:205) and presenter.letGo(). releaseBubble then calls p.reshow() (host.ts:750) or covered.reshow() (:753).
- A guide step's reshow("step") (:264).
- Unasked offers do post with { ms: OFFER_MS = 25_000, claim: "reply" } (targets/runtime.ts:478, 1137, 1227).

I ran the scratch test xreview/bubble/tree/test/unit/xreview-readtime.test.ts with vitest. All 3 tests fail:
- The task result stayed 885000 ms; the expected limit was 89500 ms.
- The offer and the answer handed back were both still up at their 10x deadline.

Nothing guards against it:
- There is no cap on ms after scaling; the clamp applies only to the factor.
- The bubble report for #51 says the intent is 10x: "Unsolicited offers then last up to 250 s". So 100x is not an accepted limitation.
- Neither lead-notes nor docs mention it.

While the bubble stays up, the reshown bubble holds it as "reply", so allows() refuses other tasks' "progress". overlay.ts:138-163 counts a finished done/idle/error bubble, or one with actions, as waiting, so Ember stays parked.

Limits on severity:
- It happens only when More time is on (the default factor is 1).
- A new user request ("take") or a dismiss still clears the bubble.

Still, every bubble that waited or was covered stays 10 times longer than intended, and longer still with each further cover. So it is a real defect, though moderate rather than catastrophic. The proposed fix is correct: scale once in hideLater, and have reshow re-arm with the already-scaled time.

confirmed.title: At the Larger text size, answers that fit six lines at 14 px lose their last line(s) with no "Read all" and no keyboard route (#12 undone by text size)
confirmed.scenario: The user picks Settings › Comfort & access › Text size: Larger (1.3). Ember answers "Your Wi-Fi is connected to HomeNet-5G with a strong signal, but the VPN called Work-WireGuard dropped two minutes ago. Would you like me to reconnect the VPN now, or leave it off until you are back at work tomorrow?" (215 chars, answerLines = 6, so cutShort is false). The bubble keeps its 300 px width while the type grows to 18.2/26 px. The answer needs 7 lines and .eb-thought's 6lh cap shows 6. The closing question is hidden under the fade, with no Read all button and no "Or press … go to Conversation." step. A six-item list ("Here are the windows you have open:" plus 5 window lines, 194 chars) loses its last item the same way.
confirmed.evidence: I built an export of HEAD (scratchpad/xreview/bubble/tree, npm run build) and rendered the real overlay page in Playwright Chromium (scripts/textsize-readall.mjs) with html[data-text-size]. VPN answer: default 14px/20px needs 6 lines, shows 6; larger 18.2px/26px needs 7, shows 6, 26 px hidden, data-overflow=true, 0 buttons. List answer: same result. Screenshot: scratchpad/xreview/bubble/shot-larger-215.png. presenter.ts:24 LINE_CHARS = 36 ("300 px wide, 14 px Ember Sans") and :37-39 cutShort take no text scale. packages/bubble/src/bubble.ts sets .eb-thought max-height: 6lh, and its html[data-text-size] rules scale the font but keep the width. page-prefs.ts:23 leaves the overlay out of FIXED_TYPE, so it scales.
confirmed.cause: fix/css #57 (text size; round 2's 2e52d11 made the caps 6lh, "whole lines at every size") merged after fix/bubble #12 (e5a5f09: Read all by answerLines at 36 chars a line). Neither side, nor the css merge 9884b6a, connects the two.
confirmed.fix: Let the presenter know the text scale. AgentHost takes textScale: () => textScale(settings.get().textSize) from main, passes it to the conversation presenter, and cutShort/answerLines use Math.floor(LINE_CHARS / scale) characters a line. Alternatively, the overlay renderer reports a finished idle thought with data-overflow and main adds ui:more. Add a pin with a 215-char answer at scale 1.3.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. The defect is real, though it covers a narrower range than "major" suggests.

What I checked:
- app/main/agent/presenter.ts:24 sets LINE_CHARS = 36 for 14 px type, and cutShort (:37-39) has no text-scale input. The only place that adds the "ui:more" (Read all) action is presenter.ts:979-982. main.ts:1256 only handles the button press. Nothing else adds Read all or the keyboard-route step.
- The bubble does detect the overflow: bubble.ts:622 and :687 set data-overflow. But nothing in main or the overlay reads it, so the overflow never turns into a Read all button.
- BUBBLE_CSS:379 scales font-size and line-height under html[data-text-size]. The width stays min(300px, ...), with no width rule in overlay/styles.css. The .eb-thought cap is 6lh (:282).
- page-prefs.ts:23 FIXED_TYPE excludes only ask, desk and mic, so the overlay page scales.

I ran the real code:
- I bundled HEAD's presenter.ts with esbuild (scratchpad/xreview/skeptic-ts/pres.mjs) and fed it userPrompt plus assistant.message. The 215-char VPN answer and the 194-char six-line list both come out with actions [] and step null.
- I re-ran the finder's Playwright render of the built overlay. The "Ember Sans" font was confirmed loaded via document.fonts, and the bubble's text area is 300 px wide. At the default size both answers need 6 lines and show 6. At Larger (18.2/26 px) both need 7 and show 6: 26 px hidden, data-overflow=true, no buttons.
- I swept prose answers that cutShort lets through (140+ chars). Default: 0 overflow. Large: 0. Larger: the 200-216-char ones overflow. List answers whose lines are about 29-36 chars also gain a wrapped line at Larger.

Nothing covers it:
- It is not in docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md L1-26.
- DESIGN.md:76-82 says only the Ask box, the desk bar and the terminal type keep their size.
- The lead-notes open items and follow-ups list the terminal font and card button min-heights for text size, not this.
- css report #57 says its 6lh caps show "as many lines at every size", but never ties that to the presenter's 36-characters-a-line count.

It is not a regression against 63b88cd, which had no text-size setting. It is #12's symptom (a hidden last line, often the question, with no Read all and no keyboard route) coming back for users of the new opt-in Larger setting.

Why it is somewhat less severe than claimed:
- It only happens at Larger (Large was clean in my sweep), and only for answers of roughly 200-216 chars or lists with longish lines.
- The bottom fade shows that something is cut off.
- The full answer is still in Settings > Conversation.

I would rate it moderate rather than major, but the scenario is confirmed.

confirmed.title: An unasked ssh offer replaces the held "Lost build-01" or "Can't connect to build-01" bubble at once, then expires and leaves nothing
confirmed.scenario: build-01 drops ("Lost build-01 [Reconnect] [Stop trying]", held, no timer), or a connect fails ("Can't connect to build-01 [Try again] [Close]", meant to stay until closed). The user opens a terminal and runs ssh to see what happened: ssh web-07, or ssh build-01 itself, whose state is lost or closed so connected() is false. The noticer, which looks only once a computer is added (remote #33), offers "You're connected to …". Its claim "reply" should make it wait, but it shows immediately in place of the Lost or failure bubble. 25 s later it expires as Not now and the bubble empties. build-01 is still lost, and its Reconnect, Try again and the reason never come back. COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md:428 says the offer "waits until you've finished reading what the bubble shows", :475 says Lost "stays until you answer it or the connection comes back", and :613 says the failure "stays until you close it".
confirmed.evidence: Scratch test appended to a copy of targets-runtime.test.ts (scratchpad/xreview/bubble/tree/test/unit/xreview-offer-lost.test.ts), using the file's own screenRig and rig with notice argv ["ssh","deploy@web-07"]. Output: "after the noticer: You're connected to web-07 [Bring Ember, Not now, Don't offer again]", then "after the offer expired: (hidden) ; build-01 still: lost". The failed-connect variant gives "Can't connect to build-01 [Try again, Close]", then "You're connected to web-07", then "(hidden)". Both fail. Code: every runtime bubble goes to the one NoticeBoard presenter (runtime.ts:664-670, nb.post), and Presenter.post replaces that presenter's previous bubble. BubbleOwner.allows returns true for claim "reply" when holder === p (presenter.ts:229), so the offer never waits behind the board's own held bubble.
confirmed.cause: fix/bubble #9/#14 (all runtime bubbles share one board presenter; unasked offers use claim "reply" to wait) against its own #11/#183 (held Lost and failure bubbles). Made reachable by remote #33: offers come only once a computer is added, which is exactly when Lost and failure bubbles exist.
confirmed.fix: Post unasked offers (showSeenOffer, offerWsl) through a second board presenter on the same BubbleOwner, for example AgentHost.offers. Claim "reply" then waits behind the held Lost or failure bubble, and the held bubble comes back after the offer goes. Or skip the offer while shown is a held key (lost:, fail:, stalled:, connecting:, or connected: with commands off) and take its key out of noticer.offered so it is offered later.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed the finding by running it. The scratch test at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/xreview/bubble/tree/test/unit/xreview-offer-lost.test.ts uses the file's own screenRig, with a real Presenter and BubbleOwner. The tree it runs in has runtime.ts, presenter.ts, offer.ts and targets-runtime.test.ts byte-identical to relfix-int HEAD; only a JSDoc comment in host.ts differs. Both cases fail:
- Lost case: "Lost build-01 [Reconnect/Stop trying]", then "You're connected to web-07 [Bring Ember/Not now/Don't offer again]", then "(hidden)" after 26 s, with build-01 still lost.
- Failed-connect case: "Can't connect to build-01 [Try again/Close]", then the offer, then "(hidden)".

The code path:
- Every runtime bubble goes through bubble(), which calls nb.post on one board (runtime.ts:664-670). main.ts:1747 wires that board as agent.notices, the single AgentHost.noticeBoard presenter (host.ts:621).
- The Lost bubble (runtime.ts:795) and the failure bubble (runtime.ts:841) post with claim "take" and no ms, so that presenter is the holder and its bubble is held.
- showSeenOffer (runtime.ts:1137) and offerWsl (runtime.ts:1227) post claim "reply" with ms OFFER_MS on the same presenter. BubbleOwner.allows returns true when h === p (presenter.ts:229), so Presenter.post replaces the held bubble at once.
- hideLater(25 s) then calls hide(), which empties the presenter's state. The replaced Lost or failure bubble no longer exists anywhere, so nothing brings it back.

Nothing guards against this:
- The noticer checks only dismissed, connected and questionUp (offer.ts:105-109). connected() counts only ready, stalled and connecting (runtime.ts:1216), so a lost or closed build-01, or any other host, is offered.
- enabled() requires hosts.length > 0 (remote #33), which is exactly when Lost and failure bubbles can exist.

Not covered elsewhere:
- docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md L1-L26 has no such limitation.
- Lead-notes' only related item is "#14 parking for unsolicited offers (bounded by 25 s)". That is about the pointer follower parking, not about bubble replacement.

The behaviour contradicts the packages' own claims:
- bubble #11: Lost "comes back after anything that covers it".
- bubble #14: unasked offers "wait behind an answer being read".
- Docs :428, :475 and :613.

Mitigation, which keeps it minor rather than refuting it:
- At 63b88cd an offer also replaced the Lost bubble through the single setter. There it stayed until answered instead of expiring, so this is an incomplete fix more than a new regression.
- Settings › Computers keeps build-01's state, its reason and Reconnect.

The minor severity stands.

confirmed.title: "More time to read and answer" doesn't reach the new notices other packages added: screen-lock notices, "I can't take screenshots", "Commands are off"
confirmed.scenario: More time is on, a setting labelled "messages stay ten times as long". (a) The user comes back to a locked screen and asks: "LOCKED_ASK" shows for 6 s (main.ts:898). The "what stopped while you were away" notice shows for 8 s (main.ts:1917). (b) macOS refuses Screen Recording mid-task: "I can't take screenshots [Open setup check]" goes after 15 s (main.ts:1547-1549). (c) The "Commands are off" hint with Open settings goes after about 10.6 s (host.ts:703). Each lasts its usual time, not ten times.
confirmed.evidence: showNotice → holdNotice(…, ms) arms setTimeout(ms) unscaled (main.ts:889-892, screen-lock.ts:276-279). The screenshots notice uses setTimeout(…, 15000) (main.ts:1547). hintCommands builds new Presenter(…, { shortcuts }) with no readTime (host.ts:703), unlike the conversation, board and task presenters (host.ts:620-622, 1414-1415). Origins: bf22035 (screen lock, voice #81), bf0de1f (screenshots notice), e74c14d (cmdcore #40). Bubble's #51 wiring covered only hideIfStill, the Confirmer and AgentHost's existing presenters.
confirmed.cause: fix/voice #81, the macOS screenshots notice commit and fix/cmdcore #40 each added a bubble after, or independently of, fix/bubble #51's readTime plumbing. No merge scaled them.
confirmed.fix: In main: showNotice(n, ms) passes ms * readTime() to holdNotice, and the screenshots timer uses 15000 * readTime(). In host.ts:703: pass ...(this.o.readTime ? { readTime: this.o.readTime } : {}) as the task presenter does.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. All three bubbles ignore More time on the merged branch.

(a) The screen-lock notices. main.ts:889-892 showNotice passes ms straight to holdNotice, and screen-lock.ts:276-279 arms setTimeout(ms) with no scaling. LOCKED_ASK is shown with 6000 (main.ts:898) and the lock notice with 8000 (main.ts:1917). hideIfStill (main.ts:534-537) is the only main-side timer multiplied by readTime().

(b) The macOS screenshots notice. main.ts:1547-1549 uses a literal setTimeout(..., 15000).

(c) The "Commands are off" hint. host.ts:703 builds new Presenter(..., { shortcuts }) with no readTime. Presenter's constructor then defaults to () => 1 (presenter.ts:534), so outcome() hides after 6000 + 106*50 = 11.3 s (presenter.ts:880) whatever the setting. The conversation and board presenters do get readTime (host.ts:619-622), and so does the task presenter (host.ts:1415).

I ran it in a scratch vitest built on host-targets.test.ts's own harness, with readTime passed to AgentHost (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/xreview/bubble-moretime/test/unit/mt.test.ts). On the ask path (host.ts:1581) the hint goes up for a moment before "Thinking…" covers it, and its timer starts then.
- readTime 1: it shows again at 6 s and hides at 11.3 s.
- readTime 10: the answer stays 60 s, the hint's unscaled timer runs out behind it, and the hint never comes back.

So with More time on, the user can lose that hint entirely, which is worse than the finding says.

None of the ways out applies:
- No guard elsewhere scales these timers.
- lead-notes "Open interaction notes" and "Follow-ups after merge" don't mention it.
- COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md L1-L26 doesn't accept it as a limitation.
- The docs promise the opposite: DESIGN.md:57 says "every bubble stays ten times as long", and README.md:213 and home/index.html:182 say "messages stay ten times as long".
- The bubble report's #51 entry says only hideIfStill, the Confirmer and AgentHost's presenters were wired.

Two small corrections that don't change the verdict. The origins are fix/perception (bf0de1f) and fix/agent (e74c14d), not cmdcore; both were merged before fix/bubble (1d44566) and neither was scaled at that merge. The hint's base time is 11.3 s, not 10.6 s.

Severity stays minor: it is an accessibility setting promised in the docs, and two of these bubbles carry the only button to the fix.

confirmed.title: The bubble names Ember's settings and stop shortcuts even while another app holds them (Read all's route, the D4.4 announcement)
confirmed.scenario: Another app holds the settings chord (or the stop chord), which ask #45 detects: shortcutsTaken, hasKey() false. An answer cut short says "Or press Ctrl+Alt+E and go to Conversation." (presenter.ts:981), and a keyboard or screen-reader user who presses it triggers the other app. An announced command (D4.4) says "… It starts in 5 seconds. Ctrl+Alt+X stops everything at once." (presenter.ts:848, target-copy.ts:145). The user presses Ctrl+Alt+X, it goes to the other app, and the command runs. Meanwhile the runtime's own routes, built from the same keyboardRoute, correctly say "Or open Ember's settings and go to Computers.", and the spoken cancel words say "Press Stop to cancel."
confirmed.evidence: Presenter's settingsKey and stopKey come from the static shortcut table (presenter.ts:528-529; AgentHost passes shortcuts: this.sys.shortcuts). keyboardRoute's contract is "`key`; null: another app took it" (target-copy.ts:155-161), and the runtime is wired with settingsKey: () => (hasKey(sc.settings.accel) ? sc.settings.label : null) (main.ts:1749). The voice cancel words check hasKey(sc.stop.accel) (main.ts:1799). Nothing passes shortcutsTaken to the presenters.
confirmed.cause: fix/bubble #47 (round 2, 80acaa6: Read all's route) and the bubble merge of cmdwin #46's stop chord into announcement() (1d44566) use the static table. ask #45 and voice V1 made the other paths shortcut-aware.
confirmed.fix: Give AgentHost settingsKey() and stopKey() callbacks from main (null while taken), and have the presenter read them per bubble. keyboardRoute(null, …) then gives "Or open Ember's settings…", and announcement() drops the chord sentence, or names the handle's Stop, when stopKey is null.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. The finding is real, and "minor" is the right severity.

1. The presenter has no way to know a shortcut is taken. Its constructor sets settingsKey and stopKey once from the static table: `this.settingsKey = (opts.shortcuts ?? SHORTCUTS.linux).settings.label; this.stopKey = (...).stop.label` (presenter.ts:528-529). Every AgentHost presenter is built with `shortcuts: this.sys.shortcuts` (host.ts:621, 622, 703, 1415). Nothing in between knows about taken shortcuts:
   - `this.sys` is `o.system ?? LINUX_WORKER_SYSTEM` (host.ts:602).
   - main passes `wslAwareSystem(sys)`, a Proxy that only swaps `apps` (wsl/privacy.ts:77-97).

confirmed.title: Renewing Ember's sign-in revokes the token Copilot is still using, and the keeper then waits up to about 58 minutes before reconnecting
confirmed.scenario: Release build with the GitHub App's expiring tokens (the GitHub default). At 7 h the keeper calls renewGrant (auth.ts:475), saves the new grant (482), then switchWhenIdle (488-494) waits for AgentHost.idle, checking every 30 s, and only forces the switch 2 min before the old token's end (FORCE_BEFORE_MS, auth.ts:379). GitHub's docs say: 'Once you use a refresh token, that refresh token and the old user access token will no longer work.' So from the renewal on, Copilot and the host still hold a revoked token. Scenario: a task is running at the 7 h mark and takes 40 more minutes. For those 40 minutes, every use of the GitHub token gets the revoked one. That covers the runtime refreshing its Copilot session token (it does so roughly every 25 minutes) and checkSignIn's getAuthStatus. It also covers every relaunch the host makes itself, because they pass this.token, which is still the old token: lost() at host.ts:1379, retryLater/retryNow at 1317/1326, and the tasks-available reconnect at 1542. The likely result is a 401: the task fails with 'Copilot didn't accept the sign-in', the host goes to error/sign-in ('Sign-in refused'), and main adds the old token to refusedTokens. That is the cut-off-mid-task outcome the idle wait was meant to prevent. Only afterwards does the keeper reconnect with the new token. The premise behind FORCE_BEFORE_MS (the old token works until 8 h) is wrong.
confirmed.evidence: I fetched the GitHub docs page (docs.github.com api/article/body for /en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/refreshing-user-access-tokens). Line 12 says 'Once you use a refresh token, that refresh token and the old user access token will no longer work'. Line 53 confirms client_secret is not needed for device-flow tokens. The existing token-renewal.test.ts:137-160 asserts this wait as intended behaviour ('waits for nothing to be under way before reconnecting', 'reconnects anyway just before the old token runs out'). confirmed.cause: fix/agent 9a3a788 (review #138, GrantKeeper): it renews first and switches later. Not a merge conflict.
confirmed.fix: Wait before renewing, not after. When the timer fires at expiry minus 1 h, wait for idle (or a forced point a few minutes before expiry). Then call renewGrant and reconnect at once (track(next) followed by d.reconnect(next.token) with no gap). Until the reconnect has happened, give the host the new token too (for example an AgentHost.useToken(next.token) that updates this.token), so lost(), retryLater() and the tasks-available relaunch never start with a revoked token. Change the two token-renewal tests to pin 'renews only when it can switch'.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute the core of this finding, but it is less severe than claimed.

What I checked:
1. GitHub's docs page on refreshing user access tokens, fetched just now, says: "Once you use a refresh token, that refresh token and the old user access token will no longer work."
2. GrantKeeper.renew (app/main/agent/auth.ts:462-484) calls renewGrant and saves the new grant first. Only after that does switchWhenIdle (486-492) wait for AgentHost.idle (host.ts:1503), checking every 30 s, or until FORCE_BEFORE_MS (2 min before the old token ends, auth.ts:379). Until then currentToken and AgentHost.token stay on the old token. main.ts:1080-1084 only changes them in reconnect.
3. With a static gitHubToken (host.ts:933), the runtime keeps sending the old token. The host's own relaunches also pass this.token: retryLater/retryNow (1317/1326), lost() (1379) and tasks-available (1542). The bundled SDK has a gitHubTokenProvider for rotating tokens, but Ember doesn't use it.
4. Nothing elsewhere guards against this, it is not a merge loss, and it is not in lead-notes' open items or follow-ups. token-renewal.test.ts:137-160 pins the wait as intended.
5. The finder's scratch test passes against the integration auth.ts GrantKeeper; the scratch copy differs only in the startDeviceFlow check.

So: if a task or answer is under way when the timer fires 1 h before expiry, its next use of the token fails. The next credential use after the renewal sends the revoked token and gets a 401. On the conversation side, the session.error triggers checkSignIn (host.ts:642, 672-688). Its getAuthStatus with the revoked token returns not authenticated. Ember then shows "Sign-in refused" and the notice "Copilot didn't accept the sign-in. Open settings to sign in again." main.ts:1771 adds the old token to refusedTokens. The cut-off the idle wait was meant to avoid happens anyway, now with copy that wrongly tells the user to sign in again.

Where the finding overstates it: "waits up to about 58 minutes before reconnecting" is not what users see. Once the 401 ends the task or answer, idle becomes true (the error phase does not count as busy). The keeper then reconnects with the new token at its next 30 s check, so Ember recovers on its own within about 30 s. The window only stretches while work stays busy without touching the token, for example a long local tool call; then the failure comes when that work next uses the token, which can be up to about 58 min later. It happens at most once per 7-hour renewal, and only if Ember is busy at that moment.

Severity: moderate rather than major. One task or answer is cut off, a sign-in error that is wrong shows for a short time, and it recovers by itself. The proposed fix is right: wait for idle before renewing, then switch at once, or give the host the new token.

confirmed.title: A computer that sleeps across the renewal time keeps the expired token for hours after it wakes: renewal runs on a monotonic timer only
confirmed.scenario: track() arms a single setTimeout for expiresAt - 1 h - now (auth.ts:457-465). Node and Electron timers run on the monotonic clock, which does not advance during suspend on Linux (CLOCK_MONOTONIC) or on macOS (mach_absolute_time). The wall-clock checks (renew() at 471, freshen) run only when that timer fires or when the user acts. Nothing pokes the keeper on wake: main's only resume hook is powerMonitor.on('resume', () => agent?.networkChanged(true)) at main.ts:1806, and there is no unlock-screen hook for the keeper. Scenario: the user signs in with GitHub at 09:00 and closes the laptop lid at 09:30 with Ember running, then opens it the next morning. The token expired at 17:00 the day before, but the timer still has 6.5 h of monotonic time left. The next request gets a 401. checkSignIn sets error/sign-in, the handle says 'Sign-in refused', and the bubble says 'Copilot didn't accept the sign-in. Open settings to sign in again.' This lasts until about 15:30, unless the user presses Check again (findToken calls freshen, which renews) or runs the whole device flow again. The same happens every morning when Ember is left running overnight on a laptop. Review #138's goal was that Ember's own sign-in keeps working without the user signing in again.
confirmed.evidence: I wrote a scratch test, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/xreview/agent/test/unit/xreview-suspend.test.ts. It mirrors a suspend with vi.setSystemTime(+14 h) while the timers do not advance, running the real GrantKeeper. Output: 'wall clock past expiry by (h): 7.5 renew calls: 0 reconnected: 0 inUse is old: true'. Only after 5.5 more hours of timer time: 'renew calls: 1'. I grepped main.ts for resume/unlock-screen hooks: there is none for the keeper. host.ts:673-690 (checkSignIn) shows that a 401 leads to error/sign-in and never to a renewal.
confirmed.cause: fix/agent 9a3a788 (review #138, GrantKeeper): the timer is never re-armed from the wall clock.
confirmed.fix: Re-check the wall clock regularly and on wake. Cap after() at a few minutes, for example min(ms, 5 * 60_000); renew() already re-tracks when it fires early (line 471). Add GrantKeeper.wake() (if this.grant, track(this.grant)) and call it from powerMonitor 'resume' and 'unlock-screen' in main.ts. Also, when main's onStatus sees reason 'sign-in' for currentToken while the keeper holds a renewable grant for it, renew and reconnect before leaving the user at 'Sign-in refused'.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. The scenario holds in the merged code, though the severity is somewhat lower than "major".

How it happens:
- GrantKeeper.track() (app/main/agent/auth.ts:454-459) arms one setTimeout for expiresAt - 1 h - now. Nothing re-arms it from the wall clock. renew() (auth.ts:468-471) checks the wall clock only when that timer fires.
- Node and Electron main-process timers are libuv timers. libuv reads CLOCK_MONOTONIC on Linux and mach_absolute_time on macOS, and neither clock advances during suspend. So the time left on the timer at suspend is still left after wake.
- The only wake hook in main.ts is `powerMonitor.on("resume", () => agent?.networkChanged(true))` at line 1806. networkChanged (host.ts:1334) only calls retryNow(), and only when the phase is already error and a retry timer is pending. At wake the phase is ready, so it does nothing.
- No unlock-screen or resume hook reaches the keeper. screen-lock.ts:173-174 only sets the lock state.
- After wake, the next request fails with a 401 or authentication session.error (host.ts:642). checkSignIn (host.ts:673-690) then sets error/sign-in and shows SIGN_IN_REFUSED with "Open settings". main's onStatus (main.ts:1771) adds the old token to refusedTokens. Nothing in that path calls keeper.freshen() or renew. freshen runs only from findToken (main.ts:1086), meaning Check again or the GitHub CLI wait, and from startBrain.
- Nothing in lead-notes ("Open interaction notes", "Follow-ups after merge"), docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md L1-26 or the agent report covers sleep or suspend. The agent report's only intended edge case is the failed save after freshen.

Test run: I ran the finder's test xreview-suspend.test.ts against the real GrantKeeper. Its keeper code matches the integration HEAD; only startDeviceFlow differs. Output: "wall clock past expiry by (h): 7.5 renew calls: 0 reconnected: 0 inUse is old: true". Renewal and reconnect happened only after the remaining 5.5 h of timer time.

Typical case: Ember is left running on a laptop. The last renewal at 14:00 makes the token expire at 22:00, with the timer due at 21:00. The lid closes at 18:00, leaving 3 h on the timer. At 08:00 the next morning the token is expired, and Ember shows "Sign-in refused" until about 11:00.

Why it is less severe than "major":
- It is not a regression against 63b88cd. Before the fix, expiring tokens were not renewed at all, so this fix is incomplete rather than wrong.
- Pressing Check again in settings recovers at once: retrySignIn, then findToken, then freshen renews and saves the grant, and the new token is not in refusedTokens.
- The keeper recovers on its own when the timer finally fires.
- Windows is probably unaffected, because libuv uses QueryPerformanceCounter there, which keeps counting during sleep.
- It still defeats the goal of #138 on Linux and macOS laptops every morning: the bubble tells the user to "sign in again".

confirmed.title: A stored sign-in renewed at start-up but not saved (disk full or read-only) is thrown away, and Ember connects with the expired token
confirmed.scenario: freshen() renews a stored grant that ran out while Ember was off, then calls this.d.store()?.saveResult(next) and ignores the result (line 447). It logs 'auth.renewed' in every case, and the renewed grant is not returned or kept anywhere. findToken/startBrain then call resolveToken, which reads the file again and gets the old token. Per GitHub's docs, that token and its refresh token stopped working at the renewal. Scenario: the home folder is full (ENOSPC) or read-only (EROFS) when Ember starts the morning after. The renewal succeeds but the save fails, Ember connects with the dead token, and the user gets 'Copilot didn't accept the sign-in'. The stored refresh token is spent, so only the device flow helps. The keeper's own renew() handles the same 'not kept' case by switching to next in memory 'for this run' (line 482). freshen doesn't, and the device flow (main.ts) also connects anyway on write-failed.
confirmed.evidence: I wrote a scratch test, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/xreview/agent/test/unit/xreview-freshen.test.ts. verdict.reason:
I confirmed it by reading the code and by running a test with a real TokenStore. Severity is minor, as stated.

Code (relfix-int HEAD, app/main/agent/auth.ts):
- freshen() at L439-452 calls renewGrant(). It then calls `this.d.store()?.saveResult(next)` at L447 and drops the result. It logs "auth.renewed" whether or not the save worked. `next` is a local variable, so it is gone when freshen returns.
- saveResult() (L135-156) writes a temp file and renames it over the old one. If that write fails, the temp file is removed and the old grant stays on disk.
- main.ts:1821-1822 (startBrain) and main.ts:1086 (findToken) both call resolveToken right after freshen, so they read the old token back from the file.
- connectFirstAccepted (auth.ts:213-229) then puts that token in refusedTokens and calls findToken again. freshen is throttled for 60 s (L443), and resolveToken skips the refused token. With no environment or gh token the phase ends as error/sign-in.
- renew() (L482-485) handles the same failed save by switching to `next` in memory, so the gap is in freshen only.

GitHub's docs (refreshing-user-access-tokens, fetched now): "Once you use a refresh token, that refresh token and the old user access token will no longer work." So both credentials still on disk are dead once the renewal succeeds.

Run: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/xreview/agent/test/unit/xreview-freshen-skeptic.test.ts, using auth.ts copied from relfix-int.
- To make the write fail I created a directory at the temp path, so TokenStore really returns "write-failed".
- The test drives the start-up flow as startBrain does: freshen, then resolveToken, then connectFirstAccepted.
- Output: `bodies 1 logs ["auth.renewed"] started ['ghu_aaa'] phase error`. Ember connected with the expired token and was refused.
- 61 s later, Check again goes back to freshen, which reuses the spent refresh token: `logs [..,"auth.renew_failed"] found null`.
- The finder's own test passes too.

Nothing elsewhere stops this:
- No other code keeps the renewed grant.
- It is not in lead-notes' open interaction notes or follow-ups. The only GrantKeeper note there is about synchronous encryptString.
- The agent report marks #138 fixed and does not mention this case.
- docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md L1-26 does not cover it.

How much it matters:
- It needs the save to fail at that exact moment: a full disk, a filesystem that went read-only, or possibly a transient rename EPERM on Windows (I did not test that).
- Recovery is one device-flow sign-in, which connects for that run even when its own save fails (main.ts:1187-1192).
- Against 63b88cd it is mostly not a regression: that commit had no renewal at all (no refresh_token in its auth.ts), so an expired stored token always meant signing in again.
- One narrow regression: freshen also renews a grant that has under an hour left (L442). There the renewal kills a token that would otherwise have worked until it expired, and Ember still connects with it.

The fix stands as proposed: when saveResult isn't "kept", freshen should keep `next` in memory, hand it to findToken and startBrain as source "stored", and call keeper.use(next.token, next), the way renew() and the device flow do. It should also log the save result instead of always logging "auth.renewed".

3. The premise about the name is strongly supported, though only a German Mac can confirm it.
   - The CI dump (mac141.log:14) shows the German entry of System Settings' InfoPlist.loctable has CFBundleName "system­einstellungen" and no CFBundleDisplayName. So the localized bundle name carries U+00AD.
   - An external report (OpenWhispr PR #2294, commit ea7f11a) says kCGWindowOwnerName "is the localized bundle name", which is "Systemeinstellungen" on a German Mac.
   - The lead's own test in 0d2717a allows that the window list may report either spelling.
   - Nothing points to the WindowServer stripping \p{Cf}.

4. It isn't covered elsewhere. It's not in the lead-notes open items or follow-ups, and not in COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md L1-L26.

Caveats that lower severity:
- (a) It isn't a regression against 63b88cd. SETTINGS_APP is new in abab066 (review #111), so on a German Mac the merged code behaves as the base did. It's an incomplete fix, though abab066's own test names German "Systemeinstellungen" as a target.
- (b) It only bites after an "Always in System Settings" grant, or an "Allow" earlier in the same task, for switches whose labels don't say security.
- (c) The isSecurityWindow/Keychain part is speculation. The finding gives no evidence that Apple writes "Schlüsselbundverwaltung" with soft hyphens, and the English "keychain access" never-look default and SECURITY_APP entries are unaffected.
- (d) The never-look miss is pre-existing behaviour, and only applies when the user types the German name.

Net: confirmed, but it's closer to moderate than major. The fix stands: remove \p{Cf} from the darwin owner name at the source, or apply apps.ts `fold` in the SETTINGS_APP test, isSecurityWindow and isNeverLook.

confirmed.title: remote.yml's new paths filter leaves out files the SSH, WSL and commands suites import at run time, so a PR to main that changes only those files runs none of those suites
confirmed.scenario: #38 put remote.yml on pull_request and push to main, filtered by paths. The commands, SSH and WSL integration suites (commands-flow-local, commands-local, remote-ssh, remote-e2e, ssh-transport, wsl) run only in remote.yml, because ci.yml's test:integration never sets EMBER_COMMANDS_TEST or EMBER_SSH_TEST. Example: a PR that changes only app/main/policy/policy.ts. PolicyEngine is a runtime import of targets/runtime.ts:41 and remote/remote-policy.ts:13, and isSecurityWindow of wsl/privacy.ts:14. That PR runs no remote.yml job at all and merges with the remote suites unrun. The same holds for app/main/policy/target-rules.ts (wsl/privacy.ts:15), app/main/policy/remote-surface.ts (wsl/rail.ts:12), app/main/settings.ts (targets/runtime.ts:49), app/main/hands/system.ts and hands/terminals.ts (remote-apps.ts, wsl/apps.ts) and app/main/environment.ts. The filter also now applies to pushes to ember-improve/20261022-sshwsl-*, which before 63b88cd ran every suite on every push.
confirmed.evidence: An esbuild metafile closure of the four remote suites over the merged tree (scratchpad/xreview/ship/closure/closure.mjs) lists sources outside the paths list: app/main/policy/{policy,target-rules,remote-surface,vocabulary}.ts, app/main/settings.ts, app/main/environment.ts, app/main/agent/confirm.ts, app/main/hands/{borrow,keymap,system,terminals}.ts, app/main/perception/elements.ts and app/main/platform/**. The grep of runtime imports (not `import type`) confirms the lines above. This release alone has 31 commits on policy.ts, target-rules.ts and settings.ts.
confirmed.fix: Add app/main/policy/**, app/main/settings.ts, app/main/environment.ts, app/main/hands/**, app/main/agent/confirm.ts, app/main/perception/elements.ts and app/main/platform/** to both paths lists. Or, more robust, drop the paths filter for pull_request and main and keep it only for the sshwsl-* branches. A unit check could compare the suites' esbuild closure with the list.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute the scenario: it is real. The finding overstates how much it matters, though.

What I confirmed in /home/user/wt/relfix-int:
- Commit 7daa539 (fix/packaging, #38) added pull_request and push-to-main triggers to .github/workflows/remote.yml. Both use the same paths list (lines 20-42 and 44-66). It also added tags v*, and GitHub does not check paths for tag pushes.
- ci.yml:62 runs `npm run test:integration` with only EMBER_VOICE_TEST set. Without their variables, commands-flow-local, commands-local, ssh-transport, remote-ssh, remote-e2e and wsl all skip. So these suites run only in remote.yml.
- The runtime imports are as stated: targets/runtime.ts:41 (PolicyEngine) and :49 (settings), remote/remote-policy.ts:13, wsl/privacy.ts:14-15, wsl/rail.ts:12. Some of these files are even imported straight from the test files: commands-flow-local.test.ts:27 imports agent/confirm.ts and :34 imports settings.ts, and commands-local.test.ts:26-27 import app/main/platform/{darwin,win32}/system/*. None of them is in the paths list.
- I re-ran the finder's esbuild closure (scratchpad/xreview/ship/closure/closure.mjs) on the merged tree. It lists policy/{policy,target-rules,remote-surface,vocabulary}.ts, settings.ts, environment.ts, agent/{confirm,presenter}.ts, hands/*, perception/* and platform/** as outside the filter.
- So a PR, or a push to main, that changes only app/main/policy/policy.ts starts no remote.yml job. The lead-notes record the path filter suppressing a run (L200: the push that created sshwsl-release started no run).

Why it is less serious than "minor" suggests:
1. For PRs and main it is not a regression. At 63b88cd, remote.yml ran only on pushes to the sshwsl-* branches, on dispatch and on the weekly cron, so no PR or main push ran these suites at all. The merged result only adds coverage. Review #38 itself asked for a path filter, with a narrower list (app/main/{commands,remote,wsl,targets}, app/remote, scripts/package), and the package delivered more than that. The workflow header also says the scope is code that "touch[es] SSH, WSL or commands code".
2. Every v* tag runs every job with no filter. Nothing can be released without these suites running on the tagged commit. The gap only moves detection from merge time to tag time.
3. ci.yml runs `npm test` on every PR on Linux, Windows and macOS (lines 52, 351, 541). That covers all unit tests, including the SSH/WSL/commands unit files that use PolicyEngine and settings.
4. The one real regression against 63b88cd is that pushes to ember-improve/20261022-sshwsl-* are now filtered too. A single push trigger cannot have different paths per branch, so this comes with the design. The feature branches are finished. sshwsl-release is now only the lead's way to trigger remote.yml, and the lead already falls back to workflow_dispatch (lead-notes L200-202).

Verdict: the scenario is confirmed. It is a CI coverage gap, not a product defect, and its severity is polish to minor. The fix is still worth making, because the suites' own test files import files outside the filter: add policy/**, settings.ts, environment.ts, agent/confirm.ts, agent/presenter.ts, hands/**, perception/** and platform/** to both lists, or drop the filter for pull_request and main.

confirmed.title: README names a Windows 11-only microphone path for a supported Windows 10, and promises an Intel Mac artifact that a packages-only CI run doesn't make
confirmed.scenario: (a) A Windows 10 22H2 user (README line 9 lists it as supported) follows README.md:84-85, "Settings › Privacy & security › Microphone › Let desktop apps access your microphone". That page doesn't exist on Windows 10, where it is Settings › Privacy › Microphone › Allow desktop apps to access your microphone. The merged code already gives both paths (WINDOWS_MIC_FIX, used by win32/system/doctor.ts and the setup check, review #100). (b) README.md:26-28 says a manual CI run with packages ticked keeps ember-packages, ember-windows, ember-macos and ember-macos-x64. ci.yml's macos-x64 job runs on dispatch only when `inputs.intel` is ticked too (ci.yml:723-725), so packages alone yields no ember-macos-x64. DEVELOPING.md §15 rightly says 'packages and intel'.
confirmed.evidence: The Windows packaged doctor output in ci.yml run 40797546710 prints the both-versions fix text from WINDOWS_MIC_FIX. README.md:85 still has only the Windows 11 path. reports/platform.json forDocs asks for both paths at README.md:44. The macos-x64 `if:` is in ci.yml.

confirmed.fix: README.md:84-85: give both paths, as WINDOWS_MIC_FIX does. README.md:26-28: say that ember-macos-x64 needs intel ticked too.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute either part. Both are confirmed in /home/user/wt/relfix-int, and both are minor documentation defects.

(a) Microphone path. README.md:84-85 gives only the Windows 11 path, "Settings › Privacy & security › Microphone › Let desktop apps access your microphone". README.md:9 lists Windows 10 22H2 as supported. The code knows the Windows 10 wording is different. app/main/environment.ts:320-325 defines WINDOWS_MIC_FIX with both paths, and its comment says "Windows 10 22H2 calls the page 'Privacy' and the switch 'Allow desktop apps to access your microphone'". The doctor (win32/system/doctor.ts:79) and the setup check (environment.ts:369) both use that constant. docs/DEVELOPING.md:752 also still has only the Windows 11 path.

The fix was requested and not applied. reports/platform.json forDocs (line 195) and the verifier note (line 307-308) ask for both paths at README.md:44 and DEVELOPING.md:731. The docs package ran in parallel and its report never mentions it. The merged diff of README.md leaves the microphone line untouched.

This is not a scheduled item. Neither "Open interaction notes" nor "Follow-ups after merge" in lead-notes.md lists it. Plan step 3 ("collect every report's forDocs lines; apply") has no commit in 63b88cd..HEAD.

The impact is limited. A Windows 10 user who runs the setup check or the doctor gets the right path; only the README text is wrong.

(b) Intel Mac artifact. README.md:26-28 says a manual run with **packages** ticked keeps ember-packages, ember-windows, ember-macos and ember-macos-x64. In .github/workflows/ci.yml:723-725, the macos-x64 job runs on workflow_dispatch only when `inputs.intel` is also ticked (and `only` is all or macos). Its upload step (ci.yml:809-812) sits inside that job. So a run with packages ticked and intel unticked produces no ember-macos-x64.

This is a regression against 63b88cd. The old README.md:60-61 said "(`ember-macos-x64` when **intel** is ticked too)". fix/docs replaced it with the new Download text and dropped that qualifier; README.md:28 is now the only place that names the artifact. docs/DEVELOPING.md §15 (line 1207) correctly says to tick both packages and intel.

confirmed.title: DEVELOPING.md's GitHub CLI install line for builds without a client id doesn't work on RHEL 8
confirmed.scenario: A developer on RHEL 8 (Ember's first platform), with a fork or a development build without a client id, follows 'Connecting Copilot': `sudo dnf install -y gh`. RHEL 8's repositories have no gh package, so dnf answers 'No match for argument: gh' and sign-in can't proceed. The repo's own source says RHEL 8 needs GitHub's repository: github-app.ts:33-36 GH_INSTALL.linux = 'sudo dnf config-manager --add-repo https://cli.github.com/packages/rpm/gh-cli.repo, then sudo dnf install gh'. Every sign-in message and the README (README.md:155-156) give that form. Commit 4e47b13 rewrote this paragraph for S1 and kept the wrong command.
confirmed.evidence: The GH_INSTALL comment in app/main/agent/github-app.ts ('RHEL 8 needs GitHub's own repository'); README.md's RHEL 8 bullet; docs/DEVELOPING.md:203 unchanged in 4e47b13's hunk.
confirmed.cause: pre-existing line kept by the S1 docs update (4e47b13; docs package)
confirmed.fix: Replace line 203 with GH_INSTALL.linux's two commands (add GitHub's gh-cli.repo, then dnf install gh), as the README does.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed, but it is minor and the scenario overstates the impact. The defect: docs/DEVELOPING.md:203 still says `sudo dnf install -y gh      # or download from cli.github.com`, and that command fails on RHEL 8.

Evidence:
- The page's own scope (DEVELOPING.md:3) says §1–§9 cover RHEL 8.4, Ember's first platform.
- I asked Fedora's package source API for gh's branches (src.fedoraproject.org/api/0/rpms/gh/git/branches). It lists epel9 and epel10.x and f34–f45, with no epel8. Bodhi has 0 gh updates for EPEL-8. RHEL 8's BaseOS and AppStream don't carry gh either. So the command fails even with EPEL turned on.
- The same release adds app/main/agent/github-app.ts (new since 63b88cd). Its GH_INSTALL.linux at lines 33-36 says RHEL 8 needs GitHub's gh-cli.repo, and the README's RHEL 8 bullet (README.md:155-156) says the same.
- This is an unapplied hand-off, not just an old line. The agent package's report (reports/agent.json "forDocs") told the docs side to give the RHEL 8 form in DEVELOPING.md §Connecting Copilot: add gh-cli.repo with dnf config-manager, then dnf install gh. Commit 4e47b13 rewrote that paragraph for S1 and kept the old line as it was. The 4e47b13 diff shows line 203 as unchanged context.
- Neither lead-notes.md list ("Follow-ups after merge" or "Open interaction notes") schedules it. Their DEVELOPING.md items are only the #147 line at :131, More time to read, and remote.yml macOS.
- docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md L1-L26 has no accepted limitation that covers it.

Why it is minor:
- The line itself offers "or download from cli.github.com". A developer who gets dnf's "No match for argument: gh" still has a way through, so "sign-in can't proceed" is too strong.
- Only forks and builds without a client id are affected. The release build has the client id built in, and CI checks that id (device-code step green on bbe8ab2).
- The line was already there at 63b88cd (line 197), so it is not a regression. It is an incomplete docs follow-through of the agent package's hand-off.

Fix as proposed: replace the dnf line with GH_INSTALL.linux's two commands, as the README does.

refuted.title: macOS Input Monitoring: the setup check, ember doctor and the README say only the keyboard is withheld, but the merged input code refuses mouse borrowing too (#65's fix left out its own README and copy alignment)
refuted.why:
The wording mismatch is real, but it isn't a merge defect, and the one part that belongs to #65 is already scheduled.

1. **Not a regression against 63b88cd.** At the base, darwin blockedReason() already refused every borrow without Input Monitoring, clicks included (`git show 63b88cd:app/main/platform/darwin/input.ts` line 419), and main.ts already fed it to the check-up. The three lines the finding quotes are word for word at the base too: environment.ts:282, darwin/system/doctor.ts:28 and README.md:78. The merge only changed the refusal text (input.ts:53). It went from "to notice when you take over the keyboard" to "...so it won't use the mouse or keyboard without it". That is more accurate than before. A refused click now names the permission and the effect, and it is the refusal that says how to fix it. No package's fix was lost or undone.

2. **The README line is scheduled.** #65's suggested fix asked only to align the README row. It said nothing about the environment.ts or doctor.ts rows. The package handed that row off through reports/input.json final.forDocs[0]. Step 3 of the lead's plan (lead-notes.md:24) is "Docs follow-ups: collect every report's forDocs lines; apply". None of the input report's four forDocs lines are in the tree yet: the README rows and the CHANGELOG entries for #61 to #66 (checked with grep). So the docs pass simply hasn't run yet. Nothing was dropped when the branches were merged.

3. **Rarely seen in practice.** The comment above INPUT_MONITORING_REASON (input.ts:43-51) records CI evidence on macos-15, runs 122 and 123. Once Accessibility is granted, CGPreflightListenEventAccess() answers true even with no Input Monitoring entry, and Ember.app's own check-up says Allowed. So this refusal shows only without Accessibility, and that case is refused first with ACCESSIBILITY_REASON. Users will rarely see the contradiction, maybe only if someone switches Ember off in the Input Monitoring list.

**What is left over:** a small, older wording polish item, not something the merge introduced. environment.ts:424 and darwin/system/doctor.ts:28 could say "mouse or keyboard". The doctor's darwin "Mouse and keyboard" row (doctor.ts:78-79, also unchanged since the base) points only to Accessibility when Input Monitoring is the cause. These rows can be fixed along with the forDocs README line.
